fields.description: Display order within the board's extracted styles.
fields.label: Index

fields.description: Driven by `decision` — Approved sets it, Rejected and Pending clear it. This is what the downstream steps (costing, ESG, techpack, the published set) filter on, so an approval reaches all of them without any of them knowing about decisions. It cannot BE the decision: a boolean can't tell "rejected, here's why" apart from "nobody has looked at it yet".
fields.label: Include

fields.description:
Whether this style is part of the moodboard the brand is shown. Default on — an approval puts the style in the board, and trimming the set is an explicit deselection, so every board written before this field existed keeps behaving exactly as it did.

Only an Approved style can carry it: a verdict leaving Approved clears it in the same save (see _reconcile_moodboard_membership), because a rejected style still flagged for the board is a contradiction nobody would go looking for. Moving back into Approved sets it again — default-on is the rule at every approval, not only the first.

Not a second `include`. `include` is the verdict's own derived flag and gates costing, ESG, the techpack and the published set; this one narrows the moodboard alone, inside what `include` already allows.
fields.label: In Moodboard

fields.description: The merchandiser's verdict on this style. Approved flips `include` on; Rejected and Pending flip it off.
fields.label: Decision

fields.description: Why the style was rejected. Mandatory when `decision` is Rejected — enforced here in the controller, not only in the dialog.
fields.label: Decision Comment

fields.description: Stamped automatically whenever `decision` changes.
fields.label: Decided By

fields.description: Main image for this garment — the current render. Accepted as a base64 data URL (decoded to a File on the way in) and offloaded to S3 on save.
fields.label: Image

fields.description:
Whether the render has landed. The page saves the styles at `plan` — 3-4 minutes before the first image — so without this a saved row with no image is indistinguishable from a failed render.

pending: no picture yet.
ready: the picture matches the current fabric.
stale: the picture is from a previous fabric and a newer render is outstanding — a stale picture beats an empty frame, so the switch keeps it.
failed: the outstanding render failed. The picture, if any, is still the older one.
fields.label: Image Status

fields.description: The cause of a render failure (product_failed.reason). Deliberately NOT `reason`, which is why the style is in the range — two different things, two columns.
fields.label: Image Error

fields.label: Renders

fields.description: Fields auto-extracted from the uploaded BOM spreadsheet.
fields.label: BOM Extracted Fields

fields.description: Auto-filled from the uploaded BOM: (Roll Width × Avg. Fabric Length × GSM) ÷ area factor, using 10000 when the fabric lengths are in cm or 1550 when in inches (unit read from the cells). GSM is read from the first fabric row's Name (e.g. "GSM-165"). Left blank if the unit can't be determined. Editable; recomputed whenever a new BOM is uploaded.
fields.label: Consumption

fields.description: Auto-filled from the uploaded BOM (the first fabric row's Efficiency). Editable; recomputed whenever a new BOM is uploaded.
fields.label: Marker Efficiency

fields.description: The fabric quality NAME (the generator's `fabricName`). The lot identity is `fab_code`.
fields.label: Fabric Quality

fields.description: The surplus lot this style is cut from (the generator's `fabricCode`). `fabric_quality` is only the name — this is the identity: the join to the board's surplus selection, and half the render cache key. Both are queries, which is why it is a column and not a key in attrs_extra.
fields.label: Fab Code

fields.description: The dye lot the style is cut in — the other half of the board's (fab_code, batch) identity (see Moodboard Surplus Fabric). Optional: empty means the style names a quality but no particular lot, which is every row written before batches were tracked, and the client falls back to matching on fab_code alone. Part of the render cache key when set, because two batches of one code are two colourways and need two renders.
fields.label: Fab Batch

fields.description: Mirrors the element_colour trio. Often empty.
fields.label: Secondary Colour

fields.description: Empty means solid. Shown on the card.

fields.description: Why this piece is in the range. Deliberately NOT `image_error`, which is why a render failed.

fields.description: Why THIS quality. Kept separate from `reason` — folded together, the fabric argument stands in for the selection argument.
